parameters.excerpt: The hardware platform may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered, as defined by the Memory-Ordering PMAs section in Volume II of this manual.
parameters.modal_signal: may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered
parameters.reasoning: The hardware platform may define certain CSRs as strongly ordered — this is a platform-level memory ordering choice. While there is clear optionality ('may define'), this is a platform/PMA-level decision rather than a pure ISA architectural parameter, making it NON_ISA. However, it does affect observable ISA behavior, so it is borderline. Classifying as NON_ISA because it is explicitly tied to the Memory-Ordering PMAs platform definition.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: If _rd_=`x0`, then the instruction shall not read the CSR and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: Fixed requirement ('shall not') binding on all implementations — no implementer choice here, just a behavioral rule.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: For both CSRRS and CSRRC, if _rs1_=`x0`, then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: Fixed behavioral rule ('shall not') — describes mandatory behavior for all implementations, not an implementer choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: Some CSRs, such as the instructions-retired counter, `instret`, may be modified as side effects of instruction execution.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: The word 'may' here is used as permission/possibility describing a class of CSRs, not as optionality for the implementer. This is a factual description of how certain CSRs behave, not an implementation choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: For the RVWMO memory consistency model (<<memorymodel>>), CSR accesses are weakly ordered by default, so other harts or devices may observe CSR accesses in an order different from program order.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This is a fixed architectural rule about the RVWMO memory model — 'may observe' is describing possible observable outcomes under the model, not an implementer choice. No optionality for the implementer.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: To enforce ordering in all other cases, software should execute a FENCE instruction between the relevant accesses.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This is a software requirement/recommendation ('software should'), not an implementer architectural parameter.
